root_cause.text: The drm/msm adreno a7xx power-up path in a7xx_patch_pwrup_reglist() unconditionally dereferenced the optional a6xx->ifpc_reglist pointer even on GPUs where IFPC is unsupported and the reglist is NULL.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (reglist)` around `lock->ifpc_list_len = reglist->count;` and the loop over `reglist->regs[i]`, while the CVE/commit message explicitly says that on a7xx platforms not supporting IFPC, `ifpc_reglist` was still dereferenced and caused a NULL pointer dereference crash.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `if (reglist)` around `lock->ifpc_list_len = reglist->count;` and the loop over `reglist->regs[i]`, while the CVE/commit message explicitly says that on a7xx platforms not supporting IFPC, `ifpc_reglist` was still dereferenced and caused a NULL pointer dereference crash.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a NULL check around ifpc_reglist handling to avoid dereferencing a missing IFPC register list during power-up patching.
intent_record.what: The code now wraps the assignment of lock->ifpc_list_len and the loop that iterates over reglist->count and reglist->regs in an if (reglist) conditional, so those operations only execute when adreno_gpu->info->a6xx->ifpc_reglist is non-NULL.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents dereferencing a NULL ifpc_reglist when accessing reglist->count or reglist->regs, avoiding a crash and allowing the function to safely proceed when no IFPC register list is present.

grouping_result.intent: Add a NULL check around ifpc_reglist handling to avoid dereferencing a missing IFPC register list during power-up patching.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by adding a NULL check before using the optional ifpc_reglist in the a7xx power-up path, preventing dereference when IFPC is unsupported and the reglist is NULL.

candidates.rationale: This directly dereferences reglist without checking whether adreno_gpu->info->a6xx->ifpc_reglist is NULL, causing the crash on GPUs without IFPC support.
The loop condition dereferences reglist->count unconditionally, embodying the same missing NULL check on the optional ifpc_reglist.
Inside the IFPC handling path, this dereferences reglist->regs assuming reglist is valid, contributing to the NULL dereference when ifpc_reglist is absent.
This also dereferences reglist->regs with no prior NULL guard, part of the vulnerable unconditional IFPC reglist access.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the first unconditional dereference of the optional ifpc_reglist via reglist->count in the power-up path. If reglist is NULL on GPUs without IFPC support, this statement triggers the NULL pointer dereference described in the root cause.
This loop condition also unconditionally dereferences reglist->count without verifying that the optional ifpc_reglist exists, so it is part of the vulnerable NULL dereference path.
Within the IFPC register copy loop, this statement dereferences reglist->regs assuming reglist is valid. It is part of the same unsafe access sequence when ifpc_reglist is NULL.
This statement likewise dereferences reglist->regs without a NULL check, contributing to the vulnerable unconditional access of the optional IFPC reglist.
